name: Coasty

modes.label: Linux running default
modes.note: Published default, per-minute rounded down. Starting/stopping/restarting also bill this rate.

modes.label: Windows running default
modes.note: Published default; effective authenticated rate card may override.

plans.name: API pay as you go
plans.note: Prepaid USD wallet; $.20 provisioning balance gate, not fee. First $5 advertised.

plans.name: Developer API
plans.note: $25 monthly API credits; same $.05 managed step; consumer credits are separate.

plans.name: Enterprise API
plans.note: Custom pricing: custom credits, dedicated VMs, SLA, SSO and priority support; no public tier (coasty.ai/pricing).

features.ip_note: Machines run on AWS/Daytona/Azure (datacenter egress); proxy {mode:'managed'} routes via Coasty's residential upstream, or bring your own http/https/socks5 proxy; no per-GB price published.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.

Public pricing headline says managed machines included, but detailed API docs and machine rate card explicitly charge runtime. Use detailed meter and flag conflict; do not assume step price includes rented VM hours.
GET /v 1/machines/pricing requires authentication (401 observed); published-default card is available anonymously at /api/pricing. No actual account-specific tariff was verified.
Stateful inference session is not a VM session and has no per-minute meter; managed machine and scheduled consumer execution are different objects.
Consumer subscription credits are quota units with variable dollar values, never the API wallet $.01 conversion. Parked-machine hourly charge cannot be encoded as per-GiB snapshot rate.
Marketing claims of benchmark superiority and comparison prices are not used as pricing evidence.

Machine size re-checked 2026-09-28: docs expose cpu_cores 1-16, memory_gb 1-64, storage_gb 8-500 ("auto" default, capped by tier) but no default size; public price feed (coasty.ai/api/pricing) lists a flat 5 credits/h Linux, 9 credits/h Windows ($0.01/credit), 1 credit/h stopped. Whether the rate varies with size is only in the authenticated /v1/machines/pricing feed, so sizes stay unpublished (vcpu/ram null).

Consumer subscriptions (separate consumer-credit balance, not the API wallet, and currently not offered for self-serve purchase): Starter $19/mo 200 credits, 1 machine; Plus $50/mo 600 credits, 2 machines; Unlimited $99/mo fair-use. Credit boosts (paid subscription required): 150/$19, 500/$49, 1,200/$99 (coasty.ai/api/pricing).

Agent inference meters are billed on top of machine runtime: predict $0.05, session create $0.10, session predict $0.04, ground $0.03, managed run step $0.05 (v1 $0.08). Surcharges: trajectory screenshot +$0.02 each, high-res image +$0.01, v1 engine +$0.03/request, prompt >500 chars +$0.01 (coasty.ai/docs pricing).

fleet.verification: API-key signup advertises no card/no subscription; provisioning needs $0.20 API-wallet balance.
fleet.notes: Consumer plans include machines/swarm agents, but this card is the separately billed API. API wallet minimum $0.20 is a provisioning gate, not concurrency. BYOK still retains concurrency and persistent-machine safeguards whose numeric default was not found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: `POST /v1/machines/{id}/snapshot` — capture a restorable machine image. Needs `snapshots:write`; the default price is `$0.01` ... Boot a future machine from a confirmed image with `restore_from_snapshot: true`.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk image only (no memory mentioned); Linux only ('Boot from your latest snapshot instead of a clean image (Linux only)'). New machines can boot from the LATEST snapshot only (no snapshot-id selection documented). $0.01 per snapshot. Managed machines only; external machines return 400 UNSUPPORTED_MACHINE_KIND.

own_agent_api.quote: A run gives the agent a task plus a machine and drives it to completion server-side: an autonomous loop with pass/fail verification, optional human takeover, managed per-step wallet billing (or zero-cost BYOK), a streaming event log, and webhooks.
own_agent_api.note: Coasty's own computer-use agent only (no Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode). The agent loop runs server-side and drives the VM via screenshots/actions rather than running inside it. API: POST /v1/runs (start with task prompt), GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (SSE, resumable), /log, /cancel, /resume (after human takeover), list runs; plus /v1/tasks, /v1/workflows, /v1/sessions and schedules. No follow-up-message endpoint documented. BYOK Anthropic/OpenAI key can power the harness.

harness_api.quote: A run gives the agent a task plus a machine and drives it to completion server-side: an autonomous loop with pass/fail verification, optional human takeover, managed per-step wallet billing (or zero-cost BYOK), a streaming event log, and webhooks.
harness_api.note: Coasty's own computer-use agent only (no Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode). The agent loop runs server-side and drives the VM via screenshots/actions rather than running inside it. API: POST /v1/runs (start with task prompt), GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (SSE, resumable), /log, /cancel, /resume (after human takeover), list runs; plus /v1/tasks, /v1/workflows, /v1/sessions and schedules. No follow-up-message endpoint documented. BYOK Anthropic/OpenAI key can power the harness.

image_oci.quote: `os_type` string no `linux` `linux` or `windows`. Windows costs more to run. ... `restore_from_snapshot` bool no `false` Boot from your latest snapshot instead of a clean image (Linux only).
image_oci.note: Provisioning only accepts os_type (linux/windows), desktop_enabled, cpu/memory/storage sizing, ttl, metadata, proxy, and restore_from_snapshot — no field to boot from a caller-supplied Docker/OCI image. Not offered: outside documented provisioning schema.

snapshot_auto.quote: `stopped` Stopped rate Powered off, disk + snapshots preserved. Start it again. ... `POST /v1/machines/{id}/snapshot` — capture a restorable machine image. Needs `snapshots:write`; the default price is `$0.01`
snapshot_auto.note: Snapshotting is an explicit priced API call (POST .../snapshot); stopping a machine simply powers it off and keeps its disk — there is no automatic state capture on stop/sleep/timeout.

fork.quote: Boot a future machine from a confirmed image with `restore_from_snapshot: true`.
fork.note: The only cloning-like mechanism is booting a brand-new machine from your LATEST disk snapshot (no memory, no snapshot-id selection, Linux only). No documented 'fork' endpoint that clones a machine directly. Treated as not offered as a first-class fork feature.

fork_running.quote: External `/snapshot` returns `400 UNSUPPORTED_MACHINE_KIND` because Coasty does not own the disk.
fork_running.note: No API to clone a live running machine without stopping it; snapshotting captures a disk image for a later separate boot, not an in-place running clone. Not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: `POST /v1/machines/{id}/snapshot` — capture a restorable machine image. Needs `snapshots:write`
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshot/restore is documented as disk-image only ('Disk image only (no memory mentioned)'); no memory state or running-process restoration is described.

wake_on_request.quote: Managed `POST /v1/machines/{id}/start` — boot a `stopped` or `error` VM. Async.
wake_on_request.note: A stopped/suspended machine only becomes running again via an explicit start API call; there is no mechanism for an inbound request to automatically wake it.

volume_attach.note: Storage is a single fixed disk sized at provision time (8-500 GB); there is no documented separate attachable/detachable volume resource. Not offered.

volume_shared.note: No shared-volume concept exists at all (only a single per-machine boot disk), so multi-machine shared mounting is not offered.

live_resize.quote: `cpu_cores` int|null no auto 1-16. Capped by tier. `memory_gb` int|null no auto 1-64. Capped by tier.
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are set only at provision time in the create-machine request; no documented endpoint to change cpu_cores/memory_gb on a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: A run gives the agent a task plus a machine and drives it to completion server-side: an autonomous loop with pass/fail verification, optional human takeover, managed per-step wallet billing (or zero-cost BYOK), a streaming event log, and webhooks.
agent_harnesses.note: Coasty ships its own server-side computer-use agent (own_agent_api), not coding-agent harnesses like Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode preinstalled on the machine.

inbound_https.note: Reachability is via a raw public IP plus SSH/VNC/websocket/devtools ports; no documented provider-managed HTTPS URL feature for reaching arbitrary ports on the machine.

ingress_rules.quote: `public_ip` string|null Public IP once assigned (null while `creating`).
ingress_rules.note: No documented IP allowlisting, security groups, or private/auth-gated URL controls for inbound access — just a public IP with fixed SSH/VNC ports gated by credential possession.

egress_allowlist.quote: `proxy` object|null no null Route egress through a proxy. `{"mode":"managed"}` uses Coasty's residential upstream; `{"mode":"custom",...}` uses yours (http/https/socks5, auth optional).
egress_allowlist.note: The only egress control is routing traffic through a chosen proxy (Coasty's own or a custom one) — there is no allow/deny list or no-internet mode documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: `proxy` object|null no null Route egress through a proxy.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented; only whole-machine proxy routing exists.

guest_firewall.note: derived: full Linux/Windows VM with root-equivalent SSH/terminal access implies nftables/iptables (or Windows Firewall) work inside, per the card's isolation model.

secret_proxy.quote: `proxy` object|null no null Route egress through a proxy ... (http/https/socks5, auth optional).
secret_proxy.note: The proxy feature routes traffic and can carry proxy auth (username/password) for the outbound proxy itself, but there is no first-party credential-injection proxy for arbitrary/AI HTTP APIs on the caller's behalf; secrets are provided as API keys (e.g. BYOK) passed by the caller.

static_egress_ip.quote: `proxy` ... `{"mode":"managed"}` uses Coasty's residential upstream ... so a proxy that is not carrying traffic fails instead of silently browsing from the datacenter IP.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/dedicated outbound IP is offered per machine; the default egress IP is a shared datacenter IP, and a fixed alternative requires bringing your own custom proxy rather than a provider-issued static IP.

gpu.quote: `os_type` string no `linux` `linux` or `windows`. Windows costs more to run. `cpu_cores` int|null no auto 1-16. `memory_gb` int|null no auto 1-64.
gpu.note: Machine provisioning only exposes cpu_cores/memory_gb/storage_gb/os_type; no GPU option or GPU pricing is documented anywhere. Not offered: outside the product's scope (a CPU desktop/computer-use VM product).

self_host.quote: Coasty AI Employee: AI computer-use agent that controls a desktop like a human (85.60% OSWorld) AND ships the best computer-use API of 2026.
self_host.note: Coasty is offered exclusively as a hosted SaaS/API product; no self-hosting distribution, on-prem package, or Docker image of the platform itself is documented. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

open_source.quote: Coasty AI Employee: AI computer-use agent... ships the best computer-use API of 2026 with a $0.05 /v1/predict base price, published surcharges, 1,000+ native app integrations, free sandbox keys, and OpenAPI 3.1.
open_source.note: No GitHub org, OSI license, or open-source claim found for the core Coasty product; it is presented as a proprietary hosted product/API. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

max_session_h.quote: `ttl_minutes` int|null no null Auto-destroy after N minutes (5-10080). Omit for no auto-destroy (adds a `Warning` header).
max_session_h.note: TTL is optional and capped at 10080 minutes (7 days) when set, but omitting it means no automatic destroy at all — the machine (a full VM) runs until you explicitly stop/terminate it, so there is no hard provider-enforced ceiling.

auto_stop_idle.quote: No-TTL warning. If you provision without a ttl_minutes, the machine will run (and bill the hourly runtime rate) until you explicitly destroy it. To make that machine-observable, the response carries an HTTP Warning: 199 - "..." header noting the machine has no auto-stop — set ttl_minutes at provision time, or PATCH /v1/machines/{id} later, to bound the spend.
auto_stop_idle.note: Machines have no idle-based auto-stop; the only auto-termination is an explicit fixed ttl_minutes countdown from creation time (opt-in, not idle detection), and the API itself warns 'no auto-stop' when ttl_minutes is omitted. Confirms auto_stop_idle: false.
